name: Synthesis Editorial Hierarchy
decision: REGRESSION; candidate not promoted; production prompt restored byte-for-byte
hypothesis: Explicitly separating Primary message, Primary subject, Supporting themes, Contextual details, and Explicit exclusions in Synthesis will preserve company-level editorial hierarchy through Narrative and LinkedIn Compose.

conditions.baseline: Three completed runs reused from Experiment 005 baseline; original Synthesis user and system prompts, Narrative, Compose, input, model and runtime configuration matched.
conditions.candidate: Three new full-pipeline runs; only Synthesis.user.prompt.txt changed. The configured response schema and all other prompts/configuration remained unchanged.

testsRestored: 165 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped; Domain test assembly had no discoverable tests
promotion: Rejected. Production Synthesis user prompt restored from frozen byte snapshot and hash verified.
limitations: Baseline runs are reused from Experiment 005 (2026-11-04); all baseline condition files and configuration were verified equivalent, but they were not rerun as part of this experiment.
No seed or temperature override is configured. Three samples are descriptive and not statistically conclusive.
The provider may change the backend behind the gpt-5-mini alias.
The console captures the selected first Idea, not all Idea candidates. Research has no configured external retrieval source.
The original workflow instruction is archived as context; the console application consumes Markdown in data/input and has no separate instruction-file argument.
The rubric scores are editorial judgments; full console logs and extracted outputs are preserved for independent review.
